label: Zyxel GS2220-28HP
description: Zyxel GS2220-28HP - 24x 10/100/1000BASE-T PoE+ RJ-45 (30 W a port, 375 W budget) plus 4x GbE combo ports, L2+ managed NebulaFlex Pro switch, 56 Gbps, 42 Mpps.

fabric.note: Zyxel quotes 56 Gbps switching capacity and 42 Mpps forwarding rate for the GS2220-28HP, with a 1.5 MB packet buffer, 16 K MAC address table, 9 K jumbo frames and 32 MB flash / 256 MB RAM (datasheet Performance table, https://static.us.zyxel.com/pdf/2024/switch/ds_GS2220-10HP.pdf; the product specification table carries the same figures, https://www.zyxel.com/us/en-us/products/switch/gs2220-series/specifications). The switching capacity is the full-duplex aggregate of the port rates - 112 ports at 1G - so it caps nothing the ports cannot already do.

notes: Census from the GS2220 Series datasheet (04/23, https://static.us.zyxel.com/pdf/2024/switch/ds_GS2220-10HP.pdf) and the product specification table (https://www.zyxel.com/us/en-us/products/switch/gs2220-series/specifications). PoE member of the 28-port pair: the 24 copper ports and the 4 combo RJ45 halves are all 802.3at PSE ports against 375 W. Twenty-eight positions at 30 W would be 840 W, so the budget is the limit and a full PoE+ load is impossible: twelve ports at 30 W (360 W) is the practical ceiling. 463.5 W maximum at the wall with a full PoE load, 25.99 W idle, two fans at 27.2/49.8 dBA. Firmware: the series spans two documentation trains. The GS2220-10 User's Guide is Version 4.70 Edition 3 (12/2021, https://download.zyxel.com/GS2220-10/user_guide/GS2220-10_V4.70_Ed3.pdf) and the GS2220-28HP guide is Version 5.00 Edition 1 (12/2024, https://download.zyxel.com/GS2220-28HP/user_guide/GS2220-28HP_V5.00_Ed1.pdf). The 4.70 guide calls the RS-232 port "for troubleshooting only" and names the default management address http://192.168.1.1 with admin/1234; the 5.00 guide opens the same port as the CLI door and moves the default management address to https://setup.zyxel (https, not http) with the same admin/1234 or a local credential in cloud mode. The datasheet (04/23) lists features marked "New for V4.80" (new Web interface, Flex link, auto configuration recovery, intuitive cloud connection status), so the datasheet describes a firmware newer than the 4.70 guide and older than the 5.00 one. Console parameters do not change across the two guides: 115200 bps, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, no flow control, VT100 emulation, male 9-pin RS-232 cable. The 4.70 guide restricts that port to troubleshooting, while the datasheet feature list offers "Management through Web interface, Console, Telnet, SNMP" and a "Cisco-like CLI" - which is why cli is modelled: telnet, SSH, web and (from firmware 5.00) console all carry it.

poe.note: IEEE 802.3af/at on every 28 PoE port at up to 30 W a port against a 375 W budget (datasheet PoE table; the user guide PoE feature table states the same budget and lists 802.3af and 802.3at both supported). 28 ports at 30 W would be 840 W, so the budget binds: at most 12 ports can carry a full Class 4 / PoE+ load at once, and the default power management mode is consumption classification, not class-based reservation. Datasheet maximum power consumption with a full PoE load is 463.5 W, minimum 25.99 W with nothing connected.
